title: Social Novelty Recruits a Dysfunctional Nucleus Accumbens Ensemble That Drives Social Avoidance in a Shank3 Autism Model.
abstract: Using the Shank3 mouse model (Jiang lab), nucleus accumbens (NAc) social ensembles were characterized with activity-dependent capture, chemogenetics, optogenetics and one-photon calcium imaging. NAc social ensembles encode appetitive cues in WT but avoidance in Shank3 mutants; mutant NAc neurons are hyperactive and hyper-modulated by social novelty. Suppressing ensemble activity during social novelty prevented future social avoidance and restored social investigation. (Abstract text had gene-name redaction artifacts; model gene is SHANK3.)
methods: Activity-dependent neuronal capture, chemo/optogenetics, one-photon calcium imaging in Shank3 mouse NAc.
summary: In a Shank3 mouse model, nucleus accumbens social ensembles encode social avoidance rather than approach, and silencing them during social novelty restores social investigation. Cell-ensemble-resolved circuit mechanism for SHANK3 (49-gene set). Descriptive mechanism, no variant data; abstract had gene-name redaction artifacts.
